norms.text: Salvage rights pass down the family and are guarded closely.
Each lot is counted at the stall before it is sold.

taboos.text: Taking timber from another family's stretch of shore.
Asking a family what it holds back from the count.

values.text: Thrift: nothing the sea gives up is wasted.

contempts.text: Buyers who haggle a lot below its price.
Talk of paying the stage-keeper again.

place.text: An Imperial stage the families keep now, under their own reed roof.

work.text: Salvage from the south shore feeds the stall and the stall feeds the families.

people.text: Two families claim the keeper's office; neither gives way.

faction.text: No guild holds the stage; the households answer to themselves.

danger.text: Fellrunners and marsh rats in the scrub; the wet coast plaster.

directions.text: The town is a short walk west; Fourth Stage lies east along the coast road.

addressTerms.text: Traveller, for anyone off the road.

neverSaid.text: What lies in the second shed.

grievances.text: No stage-keeper has been paid in two centuries.

rumours.text: A salvage lot can be traced to its ship. The owners do not know it sank.

dissent.text: Disputes the tally the stall writes for every lot his family brings in.
